rows.subtype: Noticing what was done for you [Actor]
rows.description: A child begins to see the effort behind a parent's cooking or a teacher's patience and says so. Gratitude grows from noticing effort, not from being lectured about being lucky.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 13–17, 23–26

rows.description: A teenager told to be grateful for what they have, compared to poorer children, feels guilt and resentment instead. Gratitude imposed as a weapon against complaint shuts down honest talk.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 23–26
related mind states: gratitude, guilt, resentment

rows.description: A young adult writes down three specific good things at day's end and finds attention shifting toward what works. Specific, freshly noticed items work better than repeated generic lists.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17

rows.description: A person writes or says a specific thank you to a teacher or relative, naming what they did and how it mattered. Spoken gratitude lifts both people far more than silently feeling it.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17

rows.description: A toddler hesitates at the edge of a slide, glances at a parent, then goes. Courage begins as a step taken with a safe person watching.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 23–26

rows.description: A child owns up to a broken cup even though they fear scolding. How the adult reacts decides whether honesty feels safe or expensive next time.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 7–12, 13–17, 23–26

rows.description: A child speaks against teasing of a classmate, feeling their heart pound. Courage is not fearlessness but action alongside fear, and it costs something socially.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 13–17, 23–26

rows.description: A child who stayed silent when a friend was bullied is called a coward and feels deeply ashamed. Guilt over a freeze can push toward later courage, whereas contempt pushes toward hiding.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 13–17, 23–26
related mind states: contempt, shame, guilt

rows.description: Adults watch a teenager take a dangerous dare and struggle to tell bravery from need for approval. Real courage serves a value, while recklessness serves an audience.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 23–26

rows.description: After a failed venture or rejection, a person tries again with less illusion and more preparation. Courage is rebuilt in small, doable steps, not by a single grand gesture.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 13–17
